name: TDC ADMET CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels
description: Predict whether a drug is a substrate of (is metabolised by) the enzyme cytochrome P450 2C9 (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint CYP2C9_Substrate_CarbonMangels of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the precision-recall curve on the test compounds, with class 1 as the positive class, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.

sources.locator: CYP2C9 Substrate, Carbon-Mangels et al.: binary classification, 666 drugs, merged from six publications.

Carbon-Mangels and Hutter (2011), Selecting Relevant Descriptors for Classification by Bayesian Estimates: descriptor-selection method paper whose disparate data sets include the CYP substrate sets; its main objective is the method, so it is not primary evidence.
Cheng et al. (2012), admetSAR: a database and web tool of ADMET properties; cited by TDC as second reference for the substrate sets.

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: a score that is larger for class 1 (for example its probability). train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the area under the precision-recall curve (class 1 positive) on the test part, maximized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

science_relevance.reason: The dataset paper (Carbon-Mangels and Hutter 2011) is a feature-selection methods paper that uses the CYP substrate sets among several disparate data sets; admetSAR (Cheng et al. 2012) is a database and tool paper. Neither has CYP substrate prediction as its main objective.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Classify drugs as substrates or non-substrates of the cytochrome P450 isozyme CYP2C9 from their structure.
